facts.text: Temple earned its name from a 19th‑century inn called Solomon’s Temple, whose bright sign drew travelers to the crossroads of five roads.
The original Solomon’s Temple hotel, built in 1853, still stands today as a hotel and restaurant, making it the oldest building in the village.
Muhlenberg Township, where Temple sits, was formed in 1851 from Alsace Township after settlers moved in during the mid‑1700s.
Temple’s early economy grew around iron manufacturing, highlighted by the Temple Iron Company that produced 800 tons of pig iron weekly at its peak.
The Schuylkill Canal and later railroads turned Temple into a transportation hub, linking it to Philadelphia and fueling regional trade in the 1800s.
In 1999 Temple disincorporated, ending its status as an independent borough after 77 years of self‑governance.
